results.controlIntent: a. Determine which types of changes to the system are configuration-controlled, and document those types; b. Review proposed configuration-controlled changes to the system and, with explicit consideration for security and privacy impact analyses, approve or disapprove those changes; c. Document configuration change decisions associated with the system; d. Implement approved configuration-controlled changes to the system; e. Retain records of configuration-controlled changes to the system for [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; f. Monitor activities associated with configuration-controlled changes to the system, and review those activities; and g. Coordinate configuration change control activities, and provide oversight for those activities, through [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change control element] that convenes [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; when [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change conditions]].

judgment.rationale:
CM-3.r1 requires that configuration-controlled changes (such as model deployments and endpoint updates) are approved before implementation, with records retained and oversight maintained. Cross-correlating the two evidence sources reveals two distinct violations:

**Violation 1 — CreateEndpoint temporal ordering issue (evidence 5351597d & 3d35e762):**
The model registry shows approval at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z (evidence 3d35e762). The CloudTrail CreateEndpoint event (evidence 5351597d) carries an embedded system annotation explicitly flagging that the endpoint was "Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00," indicating the deployment preceded the formal approval gate — a direct violation of CM-3.r1(b) (approve before implementing) and CM-3.r1(d) (implement only approved changes).

**Violation 2 — UpdateEndpoint with no registry entry (evidence 50f71bc8):**
A hotfix UpdateEndpoint was executed on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z by the same IAM user (data-scientist-jdoe) using config "churn-predictor-v1-hotfix." No corresponding model registry approval entry exists for this change. This means the change bypassed the approval workflow entirely, violating CM-3.r1(b) (no approval), CM-3.r1(c) (no documented decision), and CM-3.r1(e) (incomplete records).

Together, these findings demonstrate that the change control process is not consistently enforced: at least one deployment preceded formal approval, and a subsequent hotfix had no approval record at all. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of a formal Configuration Change Control Board (CCB) or equivalent body reviewing changes — human attestation needed to confirm whether an out-of-band approval process exists.
No retention policy records were available to assess CM-3.r1(e) compliance beyond what CloudTrail captures.
Security and privacy impact analyses (CM-3.r1(b)) were not retrievable from available collectors — additional documentation review would be needed.
The hotfix registry entry absence could theoretically reflect a separate registry not covered by the collector — human confirmation required.
